observation: AL1 scope ballooned from 'research-only' (original track spec: Skip /design and /architecture) to composite deliverable (research + concept + design + TSX prototypes). The 4 rounds of human-design-review drove this but the track spec wasn't updated until the concept revision. Cost: concept had to be re-locked mid-pipeline.

The 9 building-block canvases + 1 composition + 2 shared components + 1 fixture cleanly match the approved.md design table. Every canvas is tool-grounded (ToolLogo + CanvasSourceHeader) and renders 3-layer drill-down. The classification in the concept revision gives AL2-AL5 a clear 'what to build from' contract.

The 3 superseded compositions (Briefing, Stage, Focus) are in the same directory as the approved composition (Refined). A builder could import them by accident — there's no code-level guard (lint rule, @deprecated comment, or separate archive directory). The concept doc names the contract but the file tree doesn't enforce it.

Design-system tsc -b (build mode) exited non-zero on reference-noise errors (TS6059/TS6307) and failed to emit .d.ts files to dist/. The typecheck-gate script has a comment claiming 'tsc -b still emits declarations on reference-noise' but in practice it doesn't on this TypeScript version (6.0.3). Workaround: copy dist/ from primary checkout. This is a pre-existing issue on main that manifests when dist/ is cleaned.

First ship attempt shipped prematurely without concept-grounded classification. The 3 superseded compositions weren't distinguished from building blocks during review or ship. The fix (concept revision + pipeline re-run) added 2 commits of pipeline infrastructure (code review, retro) on top of the original design work. Root cause: the concept was locked before TSX existed, so it didn't classify the visual artifacts.

The design work (4 rounds of human-design-review, 2 design critiques, 3 composition variants explored before convergence) produced a clear, detailed approved.md contract. The rejection list is explicit about what was tried and why it didn't win — Briefing (floating verdict), Stage (sidebar), Focus (one-at-a-time). This is exactly the catalog that prevents future builders from re-exploring dead ends.

AL1 has no runtime tests — the TSX is visual prototypes with hardcoded fixtures. The visual verification (stories in the viewer) substitutes for test coverage, but there's no automated way to detect if a canvas regresses. AL2 production canvases will need proper Vitest tests; AL1's prototypes are accepted as visual-only.

The 27-commit iterative design process (research → 3 variants → delete-restart → 8 canvases → 4 refinement rounds) produced compelling visual output. The 6 design screenshots in plans/AL1/design/comp/ + 11 in design/parts/ provide durable visual evidence of the founder-approved state. This is higher-evidence than code review alone.

PR #333 was opened during the premature first ship and still exists pointing at the old branch HEAD. It must be closed or force-pushed-over before this pipeline run's PR opens, or GitHub will show both. Also the first ship attempt pushed 1fe0a727..9f26999c to origin/research/AL1-review-experience-dossier which is now diverged from the local branch after reset.
